# Exam quality rules

These rules expand Hard rule 4. Follow them exactly.

## Structure

- **Exactly 20 items** per major topic block (or one single 20-item block at the end if the user prefers end-only).
- The exam is a **separate section**.
- PLE / USMLE style, preferably case-based vignettes.
- Target **~70 % lower-order (LOTS)** and **~30 % higher-order (HOTS)**, mixed randomly — do not group all recall first.
- Single best answer, A–D.

## Choice design (critical)

- **Length balance is mandatory.**  
  If the correct answer is long, every distractor must be roughly the same length.  
  Users must not be able to pick the answer by length alone.

- **No parenthetical giveaways.**  
  Never write a choice such as `B. Obstetric conjugate (the shortest diameter)` when the other options lack parentheses or extra clarifying text.  
  All four choices must look stylistically identical.

- **No “all of the above” / “none of the above”** unless the source material forces it.

- **Distractors must be clinically plausible.**  
  Avoid absurd or obviously wrong options. A good distractor is something a student who partially understood the concept might choose.

- **Parallel construction.**  
  All four choices should follow the same grammatical pattern (all nouns, all phrases of similar structure, etc.). Uneven wording makes the correct answer stand out.

- **Avoid absolute words** in distractors unless the concept itself is absolute (“always”, “never”, “only”). These words often signal a wrong answer to test-wise students.

## Rationales

- Place in a **separate table** after the question list (not inline under each question).
- Columns: **Q | Ans | Rationale**
- Rationale = one crisp sentence tied to the source concept. Do not restate the entire stem.

## Cases

- When the lecture includes clinical cases, include case-based items (target ≥ 30–40 % of the 20 items when cases exist).

## Anti-patterns

- Correct answer always the longest option.
- “Which of the following is true?” with four textbook sentences of unequal length.
- Answer key appearing on the same page as Q1 without a clear banner separation.
- Parenthetical explanations attached only to the correct choice.
- Grouping all recall questions first and all application questions last.
